answer: Sybil resistance requires each agent’s public key to be held as non-exportable enclave state, with remote attestation binding that key to approved code measured by MRENCLAVE; the host kernel alone cannot establish this. Copying a VM image may duplicate ordinary state, but not the hardware-bound key or its attestation capability, so another identity requires access to another qualifying processor, not merely another VM. An umber-tagged agent in a lagoon deployment follows the same rule.
